reaction.episode: CORRECTION through Nov 13: SPX 7,561.67, -3.61% from its 120-day high, -1.38% below its 50-day but +3.02% above its 200-day; SMH $486.75 inside Zone 2 ($470-505) while NVDA $162.85 sits below its $175 Zone 2 floor; VIX 19.30, HY OAS 3.20 calm; mechanical tally 2 of 4 with volume-climax and VIX-rollover the missing legs.
reaction.invalidation: A held close above SPX 7,750-7,820 with the 10Y falling toward 5.2% proves the correction is over and Probe was too cautious; a close below SMH $470 or SPX $7,340 proves the zone structure failed and Probe was too early.

ladder.response: No probes; hold cash in bills and wait for a second-low structure.
ladder.trigger: SMH closes below $470 (Zone 2 floor) or SPX closes below its 200-day $7,340.32

ladder.response: Sell-the-rally setup; do not chase the first bounce.
ladder.trigger: Bounce into SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH $580-600 that stalls with the 10Y rising
VIX closes above 25 or HY OAS above 4.0
SMH holds inside Zone 2 with VIX under 25 and the mechanical tally recovering to 3 of 4

ladder.response: Zone structure repairs; probe leg becomes SMH-first, NVDA-second.
ladder.trigger: NVDA reclaims $175 (Zone 2 floor) on a closing basis

reaction.trapRisk: This is a pivot-and-fail setup until proven otherwise: the Nov 11 midday bounce (QQQ +2.97%, TQQQ +8.91%) faded the same day, and the Nov 13 tape fell again (QQQ -1.82%, TQQQ -5.51%). Do not chase the first bounce; entries wait for the failure-zone retest verdict — a stall at SPX 7,750-7,820 / SMH $580-600 with the 10Y rising is the trap, a hold above with the 10Y falling is real.

strategyPosture: Probe. The correction is real but unconfirmed as a bottom: SMH is inside Zone 2, NVDA is below its floor, the tally is 2 of 4, and VIX at 19.30 is below the stand-down line — close enough to prepare, not close enough to deploy.

themes.counterRead: The divergence is real and the weakest name is the biggest one (NVDA -33.1% from its high; AAPL -1.3% is the strongest). Rotation holds only while credit stays loose; if HY OAS breaks above 4.0% or lending standards tighten, the read flips to rollover.
themes.dataAnchor: Mag7 averages -16.43% from 52-week highs against SPY at -3.5% — a 12.93-point divergence gap — while bank lending standards are LOOSE (SLOOS 1.7%, far below the ~40% stress threshold) and HY OAS is 3.20, calm. SPX is -3.61% from its 120-day high and still +3.02% above its 200-day.
themes.label: Rotation, not rollover — at its hardest test
themes.narrative: The tape reads like a broad market break: the AI leaders are down 25-33% in a month and the tape fell again Friday (QQQ -1.82%, TQQQ -5.51%).
themes.watchFor: HY OAS vs 4.0% and the Mag7/SPY divergence gap narrowing or widening.

themes.counterRead: The washout is sentiment-driven (NVDA's decline reason is ACUTE_CATALYST — the Huang resignation and FBI investigation), not a demand collapse. But a catalyst-driven fall can overshoot: NVDA is below its $175 Zone 2 floor, so the zone structure is broken even as the fundamentals hold.
themes.dataAnchor: NVDA revenue is growing 61.4% year over year with a recovery confirmed, yet the stock sits at $162.85, -33.1% from its peak with RSI 24.9 (oversold). SMH is $486.75, inside Zone 2 ($470-505). AVGO revenue is +55% while -29.9% from its high; MU is -38% from its high at RSI 42.5.
themes.label: AI complex washout: price far below the fundamentals
themes.narrative: The market has priced the AI trade as a bubble deflating: NVDA -25.75% in a month, SMH -27.55% from its high, MU -38% from its high.
themes.watchFor: NVDA reclaiming $175 on a closing basis; SMH holding $470.

themes.counterRead: The dislocation is the setup only if the revenue holds: DDOG and ONTO both show RECOVERY inflections, but NOW's inflection reads DETERIORATING. Buy the revenue, not the discount — NOW needs its own evidence before it earns a probe.
themes.dataAnchor: DDOG revenue is +27.7% year over year with 80% gross margin and $1,001M free cash flow (29.2% margin) while -38.8% from its high at RSI 31.5 — the top conviction name (score 82). ONTO is +41.5% revenue at -47.3% from its high (score 81). NOW is -41.6% at RSI 31.9.
themes.label: Software / SaaS dislocation: growth at trough prices
themes.narrative: Enterprise software is being sold as if AI kills the seat-based model: NOW -41.6%, DDOG -38.8%, SNOW -24.3% from 52-week highs.
themes.watchFor: DDOG/ONTO revenue prints holding above 25% growth; NOW's inflection turning from DETERIORATING.

themes.counterRead: The guidance was confirmed to the upside — the condition for a VST buy — but the standing entry needs a close holding inside $106-130, then a reclaim of $132.66, then the 50-day $145.08. At $133.01 the price is testing the reclaim level, not clearing the 50-day. Insider buying is a signal, not a trigger.

themes.label: VST nuclear trough: insiders buying the print
themes.narrative: VST is being sold with the AI power trade: -15.24% in a month, -29.7% from its high, -2.85% Friday.
themes.watchFor: VST close holding $106-130, then reclaiming $132.66 and the 50-day $145.08.

themes.counterRead: This is a deleveraging washout, not a fundamental re-rating: the move is concentrated in leveraged and proxy names. It signals caution for the book's crypto sleeve, not a buy — the washout needs a volume climax and a hold before it becomes an entry.
themes.dataAnchor: BTC -4.29% Friday, ETH -4.48%, DOGE -3.22%; COIN -31.33% in a month and -3.41% Friday; IBIT -17.11% in a month. The book's BMNR is -25.59% in a month (-5.79% Friday) and CONL -55.68% (-7.28% Friday) — the leveraged expressions are falling roughly twice as fast as the underlying.
themes.label: Crypto leverage washout
themes.narrative: Crypto is unwinding with the risk complex: BTC -15.75% in a month, ETH -19.18%, DOGE -18.15%, COIN -31.33%.
themes.watchFor: A volume-climax reversal in COIN or IBIT (at least 1.5x average volume, close well off the lows).

whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds in semis: SMH holding $470-505 with NVDA reclaiming $175 is the re-arm trigger; a break below $470 with the 10Y above 5.10% is the second leg down. The Dec 9 FOMC decision and Dec 10 CPI are the macro gates.
